FR-G2: partly built: the kernel runs the product's suite itself and records each test's outcome, a criterion's tests must not pass on the revision before the change (fail-first), and a criterion is verified only with a passing gate and a test on main naming it (FR-G2-AC-1 to AC-3); not built: the trace and fail-first signals find a criterion's test by its name in the test files (kernel/gate.py collect_test_names) and read a test missing from a run as failing, so a naming test that is skipped, or defined where unittest never collects it, is never seen to run, yet the gate passes and the criterion shows verified; and a criterion whose test already passes at the base because earlier tasks built it is accepted when the test fails on the bare template instead. Closing it means requiring each naming test's outcome to be ok in the kernel's own run at head and FAIL or ERROR (not missing, not skipped) at base.
FR-G4: not built: no gate carries seeded defects it must catch on each run, and no gate lists its blind spots. The nearest pieces are fail-first (each criterion's tests are re-run where the behaviour is absent) and ops/seed_defects.py, the mutation script the M0 operator ran by hand for T-006's gate; no kernel gate runs it. It would take a canary set per gate (a known-bad change for the tests, trace, fail-first and verifier signals and the security gate) run with every gate decision, the gate reading not measured when a canary is missed, and a declared blind-spot list per gate recorded beside its verdict.
FR-G5: not built: gate decisions (the gate and security_gate ledger events, the deploy gate cards) record a verdict, signals and objections, but no posture. It would take a posture field set by the kernel on every gate decision, blocked before the action ran or only recorded after it, carried into the ledger, the cockpit and the evidence pack.
FR-G7: not built: gate rules have no shadow mode. The only path that adds a rule, a default check from kernel/learn.py, goes from a person's approval straight into every new contract, with no shadow phase, no replay over labelled past traffic and no false-positive limit (the shadow in kernel/operate.py replays production traffic against a release candidate, not a gate rule). It would take a rule registry with a shadow state that records the rule's verdicts beside the enforced ones, a labelled set of past gate decisions to replay it over, and promotion to enforce only after a person reviewed its false positives and the rate is under the set limit.
FR-G9: not built: the factory has no agent write release notes or postmortems, and nothing checks agent-written prose for numbers that were not measured or causal wording without a supported result. It would take a checker that extracts each number and causal claim from such text and fails it unless a ledger record or a measured result backs it, run as a gate before the text is published.
